column2: req_desc

Exact starting seed
A fresh install shows exactly the farms, sites, pens, defects, repair, dive, report revision and devices listed in Seed data, with the derived values printed there, and nothing else.

Pen condition cards
The Pens page shows one full-width card for the open pen, then one square card per pen, each with a procedural still of its own twin, its name and its server grade line, and the hover and keyboard-focus reveal described in Motion and effects. Cards change in place when the other device changes a pen, the card or button with keyboard focus keeps it, and an erased farm's row and cards leave the page in place.

Live pen twin
The workspace stage renders a live 3D twin of the selected pen (net wall, collar, moorings, light shafts, particles, at most 60 fish and the ROV) with one pin button per defect, and falls back to the flat chart without WebGL, as described in Motion and effects.

Pen Unwrap and Wrap
Unwrap lays the net wall flat into the metre-true chart over elapsed time, ending with every pin at its server chart position and the Scene status reading the flat-chart view, and Wrap reverses the same path back to the cylinder. Pressing the opposite control mid-run plays the progress made so far back at the pace it was made, so a run reversed 0.5 seconds after it started is back in its starting view 0.3 to 0.8 seconds later.

Keyboard pen twin
The published shortcuts orbit, zoom, unwrap, wrap, step through defects with a camera fly-to and open the editor from any focused control in the workspace, and are ignored while typing, while a dialog is open and, for the arrow, Home and End keys, while focus is on a tab. Tab follows the published workspace order at the laptop and tablet sizes, and Escape, Close editor or a successful delete closes the editor and returns focus to the pin or row that opened it, or to the placeholder row after a delete.

Touch orbit, pinch and tap
On a touch screen one finger orbits the cylinder or pans the flat chart, two fingers pinch-zoom and a tap on a pin selects its defect, and the Scene status shows the result.

Reduced motion end states
Under the reduced-motion preference every ambient loop stops and Unwrap, Wrap and camera fly-to show their end state in a single frame, while orbit, pinch, drag and the dive clock keep working.

Server-computed defect position
The server turns each typed bearing or tapped net-wall point, together with the depth, into the stored bearing, depth, chart x, chart y and panel cell by the rules in Business rules, and the browser shows only those values.

Defect sizes and fouling cover
The server computes hole, tear and chafe areas and each panel's fouling cover, splitting fouling patches at panel boundaries and across the reference seam, with the published formulas and rounding.

Pen condition grade
The server grades each pen from its open defects and fouling cover by the published grade rule, and every surface shows that grade.

Note length as people count it
Notes, private notes, repair notes and copilot questions are limited in user-perceived characters, with an emoji or a flag counting as one; the API refuses one character over the limit, and the editor's counter shows the same count.

Stills and sonar captures kept byte for byte
Stills and sonar captures within their size limits are stored in MinIO and download with exactly the uploaded bytes and the published SHA-256, and uploads over the limits are refused as described in API.

Mark a defect from the twin
The inspector enters marking mode, taps the net wall, fills in the editor and saves, and the new defect's pin, list row and cell and the pen's grade appear from the server's reply. Marking mode and a half-filled New defect editor, with its typed values, focus and caret, survive a change the other device makes to the same pen.

Edits reach every surface
Editing or deleting a defect updates its 3D pin, its flat-chart position, its list row, the farm manager's report link and the next report pack.

Defect history and removal placeholder
Every change to a defect writes a history entry naming the device and the before and after values, and a deleted defect remains everywhere as a 'Defect removed' placeholder carrying its id.

Live updates on the other device
A change saved on one device moves the pin and updates the list row on the other open device in place, with no reload, within the published delay, and the 'Console updates' live region announces it. The camera, selection and keyboard focus stay where they were, and a repair made on the other device is announced with the published copy.

Defect edit locks
Opening the editor takes a short-lived edit lock in Valkey that is refreshed while the editor stays open, and saves, deletions, repairs and still uploads from any other device are refused until the lock is released or expires. When a refresh is refused because the lock was lost, the editor shows the lock-lost copy and keeps the inspector's unsaved input.

Device presence and lock indicator
Each open console sends heartbeats, the Devices page shows each device Online or Offline as the server decides, and the other device shows 'Being edited on <device name>' while a lock is held.

Editor survives earlier timers
Reopening the defect editor while it is closing, or after a toast or lock-refresh timer from an earlier session has started, never hides the reopened editor, never refreshes a released lock and never overwrites the newer status message.

Dive planning and forecast request
The inspector plans a dive for a pen, and a forecast check calls the marine forecast provider with the site's position and the planned hours exactly as published in Services.

Clearance rules
The server decides GO, NO-GO with the first failing hour and value, or 'Forecast stale' from the provider's hourly values and issue time against its own clock, by the limits in Business rules.

Start dive needs a fresh GO
Starting a dive succeeds only when the dive's latest clearance is a GO that is still not stale on the server clock at the moment of starting, and it is refused otherwise.

Clearance shown as the server decided
The Dives page and the report link list show the clearance and link status the server returns and never recompute either from the device clock, which may be wrong. The dive clock counts up from the server's elapsed seconds, and an open planned or cleared dive whose GO has become more than 6 hours old reads stale after the page's next 30-second refresh.

Forecast outage and newest check
When the forecast provider errors, sends unusable data or does not answer in time, the check is recorded as 'Forecast unavailable' with the published status, and a reply to an earlier check never replaces a newer check's result.

Dive day from plan to recorded
The inspector plans a dive, checks the forecast to GO, starts the dive with the dive clock running, finishes it with track samples and sees it recorded with its track.

Copilot answers and camera focus
Asking the copilot sends the question and the pen's findings to the chat-completion provider, shows the answer and flies the camera to the defects its focus tool call names, and a reply to an older question never replaces a newer answer. An answer that arrives after another pen was opened is dropped, and a repair applied from a proposal reaches the other open device like any other repair.

Validated repair proposals
Repair proposals exist only from valid propose_repair tool calls, unknown or removed defect ids are dropped and listed, every other bad call is rejected with one published reason, and applying the same proposal twice records one repair.

Copilot unavailable, manual repair works
When the chat-completion provider errors, sends a malformed reply or is too slow, the copilot shows 'Copilot unavailable' and manual repairs keep working.

Legacy log matching
Importing a CSV log from the older inspection tool matches pens by site code and pen number under the published rules, merges nearby same-type marks into existing defects, creates the rest and reports orphan and invalid rows with their row numbers.

Re-import creates nothing
Importing the same file again, or a file whose rows were already imported, creates no defect, and the raw file is kept in MinIO byte for byte and downloads with its SHA-256. A file the other device imports shows its new defects in place on an open workspace of that pen and joins the Imports page list in place.

Numbered report revisions
Publishing a report creates the pen's next numbered, immutable revision, whose pack is stored in MinIO and downloads byte for byte with its published SHA-256.

Exact revision restore
Restoring a pen to a past revision brings back exactly that revision's defect ids, positions, sizes, notes, statuses, repairs and still attachments. While another device holds the lock on one of the pen's defects, Publish revision and Restore revision print the lock copy and change nothing, and a newly published revision appears in place on the other device's Reports page.

Reports page bands and counters
The Reports page shows the latest report row, the grade and open-defect counter panels and one band per revision with its flat chart, each revealed once on scroll as described in Motion and effects.

Report link lifecycle
The inspector creates a read-only report link with a chosen expiry, regenerates it so the old token stops working at once, and revokes it so it stops working at once; the link counts as expired from the server moment it reaches its expiry, its remaining time prints in whole hours and minutes rounded down, and every write through a link is refused.

Share a report with the farm
The inspector publishes a revision and creates a report link, the farm manager opens it and sees the pen, grade and defects, and after revocation the link shows the inactive message while every inspector device shows it as revoked. Links created, regenerated or revoked on one device update the other device's rows in place within the live-update delay, with the published announcement copy and without moving its keyboard focus. The list's 30-second refresh updates each row's remaining time in place and keeps keyboard focus and the caret where they were.

Report link privacy
The report link's HTML, JSON and scene data never contain the day rate, private notes, the diver certificate number, device names, lock data or history.

Farm manager report view
The report link page lets the farm manager orbit, unwrap and select pins and read the grade and defect list in its phone, tablet and laptop layouts, with no editing control. Each 15-second re-check updates only what changed and keeps the selected tab, the selected pin unless its defect was removed, the camera and keyboard focus.

Search and defect export
The console searches farms, pens and defects and exports every current defect as CSV with the published columns.

Farm erasure
Erasing a farm after typing its name removes it and everything under it from the console, search, exports, report links and MinIO, and an open report link page of that farm shows the does-not-exist message at its next re-check. The Erase farm dialog opens with focus on Cancel, Escape closes only that dialog and returns focus to Erase farm in Farm details, and the other device's Pens page drops the farm's row and cards in place.

Published layouts
Each screen shows its published arrangement at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800, with nothing overlapping, cut off or scrolling sideways.

Dialogs and focus
Every dialog keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside it, closes on Escape and returns focus to the control that opened it, and every action works by keyboard with a visible focus ring. A dialog opened from inside another dialog closes alone on Escape, and every download link saves a file with exactly the stored bytes without leaving the page. The Keyboard shortcuts dialog that ? opens on the report link page follows the same rules.

One error shape
Every refusal uses the one published error JSON shape, the exact status code for its cause and the published precedence. A call that never reaches the server prints the unreachable copy, and the inspector's typed input stays.

Health and boot
The server answers its health check, applies its schema and seed idempotently on every start, and keeps serving the console when the third-party providers are unreachable.

Abyssal, clinical console look
The console is near-black, with white type, white pins and white tabular figures with their units; colour appears only in the water and in the stone, paper and olive report fields, and the layout follows the composition in Visual design.

Real services behind every state
Every record, file, heartbeat, lock and broadcast lives in Postgres, MinIO or Valkey as published, the providers are called over HTTP at the configured base URL, and no credential reaches the browser or appears in the source.

First-open copy verbatim
A fresh install shows the grade lines, day rates, Devices header and rows and Scene status lines listed under First-open copy in Seed data character for character, including the dash, the middle dot and the singular and plural defect counts.

Imports applied one at a time
Imports of one farm are applied one at a time in arrival order, so two simultaneous byte-identical uploads give one created import and one replay with the same import id, and a row shared by two simultaneous files creates its defect exactly once.

Regenerate has one winner
Regenerating a report link requires the token the device shows, a stale token is refused with the published 409 copy while the list refreshes in place, exactly one of two simultaneous regenerates wins, and a regenerate racing a revoke always ends revoked with every token refused.

Tabs and collapsed panels
The phone 'Pen panels' and 'Report panels' tab lists follow the published arrow-key, Home and End behaviour without orbiting the camera, and every unselected tab panel, collapsed footer column and closed menu is hidden, unfocusable and absent from the accessibility tree.

Formula-safe defect export
The defect CSV export writes a leading apostrophe before any text cell that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return, while stored notes, the API, the report link, report packs and raw imports keep the original text.

Search shows the newest input
The Search dialog's results and 'Search status' always describe the text now in the box, a late reply to an earlier query is discarded, and under 2 characters the status asks for more. Choosing a defect result opens that pen's workspace at its canonical address with the defect selected and the camera facing it.

Workspace address holds view and selection
The workspace address records the settled view and the selected defect without adding history entries, and loading such an address shows that end state in a single frame with the published Scene status lines, dropping unknown or removed defect ids and reading any other view value as the cylinder.

Bounded literal search
Search text is trimmed and holds at most 100 user-perceived characters, 101 gets the published 422, and every character, including %, _ and the backslash, matches literally.

Copilot request carries only the findings context
The chat-completion request holds exactly two messages, the published findings context with exactly eight keys per non-removed defect and the question exactly as asked, and never a private note, day rate, certificate number, device, lock, version, still, history or Authorization header.

Simultaneous defect writes have one winner
Writes to one defect are applied one at a time, so of simultaneous saves, repairs or deletions exactly one is applied, the others get the published 409, and no write lands after a removal.

Report link countdown from the server
The report link page prints its expiry line from the server's expires_in_s at load and at each 15-second re-check, and shows the inactive message within 20 seconds after expiry, whatever the phone's clock reads.

Cross-site writes refused
Any POST, PATCH or DELETE under /api whose Origin is present and foreign, including null, gets the published 403 and changes nothing, and no response carries cross-origin allow headers.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and those commands alone install, build and serve the app.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package with its licence; shipped packages means the crates of the normal, non-dev Rust dependency graph, plus the production npm tree (npm ls --omit=dev --all --json), plus the bundled fonts and icons.
Shipped packages and assets use only the MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-3.0, MPL-2.0 and CC0-1.0 licences, plus OFL-1.1 for fonts.
The app uses no datastore beyond Postgres, MinIO and Valkey: no SQLite, no embedded database and no state files on local disk.
Cargo.lock and the npm lockfile are committed, and the build installs no system library beyond build-essential.
The app itself serves the fonts (Inter and Inter Tight), three.js and the icons, and the browser loads nothing from another origin.
The provided service configuration files are left unchanged.
